newsitem.title: UK: UK telecoms watchdog bans BT/BSkyB promotion.
newsitem.headline: UK telecoms watchdog bans BT/BSkyB promotion.

text.p: Regulator Oftel ruled on Tuesday that a joint marketing campaign between British Telecom and satellite broadcaster BSkyB was in breach of BT's licence and issued a provisional order against it.

Oftel head Don Cruickshank said he would examine whether or not BT had breached conditions on advance publication of its charges and prohibition of linked sales before deciding whether to confirm the provisional ban.

"BT is paying for the television advertising and certain other marketing costs of a special offer under which members of its Friends and Family Scheme may qualify for discounts on both their BT telephone bills and BSkyB's television service," Cruickshank said.

"The promotion offers a refund of a substantial part of a typical residential consumer's telephone bill. The arrangements are made between BT and the only provider of multi-channel television services with which it is not in competition.

"The offer will benefit only the small range of customers who are prepared to incur the expenditure necessary to receive BSkyB's TV services," he added, saying the initiative distorted competition in the supply of telephone services.
A BT spokesman said the company was complying with the order to stop the promotion.
But he added: "We cannot fathom the Director General's conclusion that the promotion shows undue discrimination or preference between groups of BT customers."
